facts.text: Avon, Montana, takes its name from the Welsh word for river, reflecting the Little Blackfoot River that flows through the valley.
In 1884, Bill Cramer returned with homesteaders, founded Avon, and became its first postmaster.
The Anderson Phosphate Mine, later called Cominco, operated in the early 1940s and employed up to 150 workers before closing in the 1970s.
Avon grew into a supply and shipping hub for ranchers, homesteaders, and miners after the transcontinental road linked the town to the rail network.
The Community Hall in Avon remains a living historic building where congregations still gather and laughter echoes through its walls.
Avon's Fitzpatrick Ranch Historic District is listed on the National Register of Historic Places, preserving its 19th-century ranching heritage.
